If a block does not compile, the divergence is in your transcription or a changed dependency, not in the plan. Run `cargo fmt` before `cargo fmt --check` (plan blocks are not all rustfmt-formatted).

title: Task 3: Jev client with retries, concurrency, disk cache, prewarm
description:
Outcome: The Jev HTTP client (`Client::new/ask/prewarm`) with retries, a concurrency semaphore and a blake3-keyed 7-day disk cache; the shared test harness `tests/common/mod.rs` (FakeJev over wiremock, `bin()`, `hunch()`, `config()`, `option_containing()`); `tests/client.rs` (3 tests) passes; committed and pushed.

The plan holds the verbatim, compile-verified code; copy it exactly, do not redesign. Run `cargo fmt` before `cargo fmt --check`.

Context:
- Consumes (Task 2): `config::Config` (pub fields; `api_key()`, `base_url`, `model`, `concurrency`, `cache_dir`, `stats`), `jev::{Questions, Response}`, `jev::client::Stats` (already in client.rs — append the client below it), `HunchError`.
- Produces: `jev::cache::key(&[u8]) -> String` (blake3 hex); `jev::cache::DiskCache::{new(PathBuf) -> io::Result<Self>, get(&str) -> Option<Response> (ignores entries older than 7 days; path `<dir>/answers/<k[..2]>/<k>.json`), put(&str, &Response) (best effort: tmp file + rename; a failed write never fails the command)}`; `jev::client::Client::{new(&Config) -> Result<Client, HunchError> (calls `Config::api_key`; reqwest client with connect timeout 5 s, timeout 60 s, pool idle 90 s, user-agent `hunch/<version>`), prewarm(&self) (tokio::spawn a GET `{base}/v1/models` with bearer auth and read the body so hyper returns the connection to the pool), async ask(&self, state: &serde_json::Value, questions: &Questions) -> Result<Response, HunchError>}` posting `{ "model", "state", "questions" }` to `{base}/v1/systemone` with bearer auth, content-type application/json, under the semaphore, cache lookup before the network (cache hit increments `stats.cache_hits` and sets `stats.model`). Test helpers: `common::FakeJev { choose: fn(&str, &Value, &[String]) -> String, noul: fn(&str, &Value) -> f64 }` implementing wiremock `Respond` (picked option gets 0.9, the rest share 0.1; model "jev-fake", usage input_tokens 100); `common::mock(FakeJev) -> MockServer` (POST /v1/systemone + GET /v1/models); `common::bin() -> assert_cmd::Command` with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE, HUNCH_BASE_URL, HUNCH_THRESHOLD, HUNCH_MODEL, HUNCH_CONCURRENCY, HUNCH_CACHE_DIR, HUNCH_NO_CACHE, HUNCH_PRICE_PER_MTOK, HUNCH_NO_PREWARM, HUNCH_INVENTORY_FILE removed; `common::hunch(&MockServer)` (bin + HUNCH_BASE_URL=server, TYPESAFE_API_KEY=test-key, HUNCH_NO_CACHE=1); `common::config(&MockServer) -> hunch::config::Config` built literally (model jev-1.13.0, threshold 0.5, concurrency 8, no cache, prewarm false); `common::option_containing(state, opts, needle) -> String` (the `[Lnnn]` id of the `state.items` entry containing needle, else "NONE").
- HTTP mapping (copy exactly): 200 → parse `Response`, bump `stats.requests` and `stats.input_tokens`, set `stats.model`, cache put; 401/403 → `BadKey` (exit 5); 413/422 → `RejectedRequest(status, body[..300])` (exit 6, kind api_rejected_request: state over the token budget, or occasionally a malformed request which is a hunch bug — neutral message, hint covers both); 408/429/5xx (incl. 529) → retry (loop `0..4`, sleep 250 ms * 2^(attempt-1) before retries, plus `retry-after` seconds capped at 10); reqwest timeout/connect errors retry, other reqwest errors → `Unavailable`; any other status → `Protocol` (exit 4) with body[..300]; exhausted → `Unavailable(last)`.

Operation not permitted") and every `git commit`/`git push` run with the sandbox disabled; never #[ignore], weaken or delete a test to get past a sandbox failure; never read/print/copy ~/.ssh; never delete files; treat unexplained working-tree changes as another agent's work: never stash, revert or overwrite them; commit only your own paths. title: v0 acceptance: live CLI test, install from source, README numbers, push, tag v0.1.0
description:
Outcome: v0 is verified end to end on this machine and published: a live CLI test of every v0 verb (pick, why, run, is, capabilities, health, robot-docs, init) with the real key, install from source, README numbers present, full gate green, `origin main` pushed, and — if the release pipeline exists — the first green release tag `v0.1.x` (v0.1.0, or v0.1.1 if the v0.1.0 run failed; see "Tag and release") pushed with verified assets. This is the cut line: wave 2 (Tasks 14–15) starts only after this bead closes.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — the header ("Launch cut line"), "## Global Constraints", "### Task 16: Release — binaries, launch checklist (Homebrew tap and Show HN optional, user-gated)" Step 3, and "## CUT LINE — v0 is public before anything below starts"; README.md, PRIVACY.md and docs/ROBOT_MODE.md as shipped.

Context:
- Authorization (lead note): the plan marks Task 16 Step 3 "(needs Thomas)". Thomas explicitly authorized publishing a public v0 while AFK — "push it to the public remote ... v0 online and public" (2026-09-19) — and the repo tpellet/hunch is already public. That authorization covers the tag and the release below; no further approval is needed. It covers a verified v0 only: this bead does not close unless every live check below actually passed.
- Live test — sandbox DISABLED, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key` in each command's environment (hunch reads the file; you never read, print, copy or echo it). The per-verb matrix below is this bead's acceptance contract (the plan's Step 3 names only health, one `why`, one `pick`, one `run --dry-run`; the rest is lead-added). `cargo build --release`; `H="$PWD/target/release/hunch"` (absolute: two checks below run from another directory). Run and record exit code + one-line output for each:
  - `$H health` and `$H health --json` → 0, key accepted; `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=wrong $H health` → 5.
  - `$H capabilities --json` → 0; commands are exactly pick, why, run, is, capabilities, robot-docs, health, init (no add/sort); HUNCH_MODEL default jev-1.13.0.
  - `$H robot-docs`, `$H robot-docs privacy` → 0; `$H robot-docs nope` → 2.
  - `ls /usr/bin | $H pick "compress files"` → 0 and prints a real /usr/bin name; `printf 'a\nb\n' | $H pick "a spaceship"` → 3, empty stdout; `$H pick x < /dev/null` → 6.
  - `$H --json why -- sh -c "echo ok; echo 'error[E0432]: boom' >&2; exit 1"` → 0, cause text contains E0432, `data.child_exit == 1`; `$H why < benchmarks/fixtures/cargo-fail.log` → 0 with a `>` marked line.
  - `echo "I want my money back" | $H is "asks for a refund"; echo $?` → 0; `echo "hello" | $H is "asks for a refund"; echo $?` → 1 or 3; `$H is --band 0.9 x < /dev/null` → 2.
  - `$H run --dry-run "extract the gzipped archive"` → 0, proposes tar/bsdtar/gunzip/gzip, not executed; `$H --json run --dry-run "make a qr code"` → 3 unless something installed does it; the two `list files` checks run from an empty scratch directory (`cd "$(mktemp -d)"`, absolute `$H`) so argument pointing cannot pick up repo file names: `$H --json run --yes "list files"` → executed false (no --exec); `$H --json run --exec --yes "list files"` → executed true, stdout is exactly one envelope; `$H --json run --dry-run "delete the temp file"` → `data.tool` is `rm` or another deleter, `data.blocked` non-null, `data.executed == false`, nothing run (use `--json`: in human mode `blocked` is only a stderr sentence and is printed only when the proposal is complete).
  - `zsh -ic 'eval "$(./target/release/hunch init zsh)"; alias ,'` and `bash -ic 'eval "$(./target/release/hunch init bash)"; alias ,'` each show the `,=` alias (no TTY is available; `-ic` is the form to use).
  - `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key cargo test --test live -- --ignored --test-threads=1` → both live tests actually run and pass (a SKIPPED line means NOT RUN — fix the environment, do not accept).
  Two kinds of check, two rules (lead decision, pass 2). Deterministic contract checks — exit codes 2/5/6, the envelope shape, `executed`, `blocked`, the alias, the capabilities list, `data.child_exit`, the abstain path on fake input (`a spaceship` → 3), the live tests — must pass: a failure there is a code defect; fix in place with the gate and a commit `fix: <what> (hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2)`, or report NOT ACCEPTED with the evidence and leave the bead open. Model-judgment checks — `is` refund → 0, `why` naming a cause / E0432, the `pick "compress files"` name, the `run` proposals (tar family, qr → 3, rm for "delete the temp file"), `hello` → 1 or 3 — get exactly one re-run with `--no-cache`; a miss that persists is recorded verbatim (command, exit code, output) in the close reason and with `br update hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "<miss>"`, and, if it is not already there, added to README "What it is bad at" (commit `docs: record v0 acceptance miss (hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2)`); it does not block acceptance. Never change prompts, constants, `WINDOW`, the threshold or any calibrated surface in this bead to "fix" one example. Only if every model-judgment check misses is it a code defect (the pipeline, not the model): investigate, fix in place or NOT ACCEPTED. If the API or network is down, append the error with `br update hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "<error>"`, leave the bead open and stop; retry later. There is no NOT RUN close for this bead.
- Install from source, into a scratch root — never the real `~/.cargo/bin` (the sandbox denies it and Thomas's own `hunch` must not be overwritten): `cargo install --path . --locked --force --root "$TMPDIR/hunch-root"`, then `"$TMPDIR/hunch-root/bin/hunch" --version` prints `hunch <Cargo.toml version>` (0.1.0, or 0.1.1 under the re-release path below) and `"$TMPDIR/hunch-root/bin/hunch" capabilities --json | head -3` works; after the push, `cargo install --git https://github.com/tpellet/hunch --locked --force --root "$TMPDIR/hunch-root"` also works from this machine (sandbox disabled if the fetch is refused).
- README: every 13b section present; "Numbers" holds measured tables (no "pending" for speed/run/why — if a live-step follow-up bead is still open, this bead is blocked by it and cannot start); Install shows the installer command (Task 16) or the `cargo install --git` form; the independence sentence is present; demo.gif referenced. The GIF review is not a gate for this bead (Thomas's public-v0 authorization covers it); list "demo.gif awaiting Thomas review" in the close reason and the hand-off.
- Full gate (sandbox disabled): `cargo fmt --check && cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test -- --test-threads=1`; `ubs` on any file you changed (outside the sandbox; exit 0; verify warnings, fix genuine bugs, list the rest in the close reason).

If it is somehow private, do NOT change visibility yourself: report NOT ACCEPTED and leave the bead open — the plan's cut line requires a public repo before wave 2.
- Tag and release (authorized above): if `.github/workflows/release.yml` exists (Task 16). Before tagging: `dist plan` (install `dist` per the Task 16 bead if it is missing, sandbox disabled) must list `hunch` archives for the configured targets and the shell installer; if it lists none, stop, report NOT ACCEPTED, append the output with `br update hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "<dist plan output>"` and do not tag (the Task 16 bead's `dist = true` is missing). Tag: `git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "hunch 0.1.0"` on the accepted commit; add `-s` only if `git config tag.gpgsign` is already true or tag signing already works with the existing config (`tag.gpgsign` was unset on 2026-09-19; commits are SSH-signed) — otherwise an unsigned annotated tag is acceptable; never change signing config, never bypass signing that is configured; record signed/unsigned in the close reason. `git push origin v0.1.0` (sandbox disabled); `gh run watch` the release workflow until it ends (outside the sandbox); verify the GitHub release assets exist for the configured targets and that the shell installer command from the README works and yields `hunch --version` with the tagged version — on a clean macOS user account if Thomas provides one, otherwise as `env HOME="$TMPDIR/home" CARGO_HOME="$TMPDIR/home/.cargo" sh -c '<installer command>'` with the installer's no-modify-path variable set (read its name from the generated installer script before running it; never run the installer against the real HOME), and say which in the close reason. Debian check: `docker` is not installed on this machine (checked 2026-09-19) — record "debian:stable-slim check NOT RUN (no container runtime)" in the close reason; if a container runtime exists, run the linux binary in `debian:stable-slim` with the key bind-mounted read-only (`-v $HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key:/run/key:ro -e TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/run/key`, never copied or echoed): `hunch health`, one `why`, one `pick`, one `run --dry-run` (no man pages: `run` must still route by name).
